Fixed it today. Was a bitch and a half. There were 8 bolts holding the long bed to the frame, plus took off the ground, the fuel inlet, the taillight cables, the tag light cables, and took the tailgate off to make it lighter, took the bumper off to allow the bed to slide off back and tilt (6 bolts). Lifting it off was cumbersome, but not too heavy for two (even the 8ft long bed), no where to grip so we used tie down straps hooked under bottom. Rested it of the tires protected by scrap wood.

Got the volt meter and did a voltage check. The plug had 4 wires, but there were only 2 heavy guage wires, it showed 12v at ON for a second so I knew it was getting juice and it wasn't relay or anything, when I disconnected the fuel line to the pump there was no "squirt" so no pressure, so didn't bother picking up a pressure gauge. Picked up a $200 fuel pump/filter assembly, vacuumed the area around it so no debris could fall in tank, snap ring came off put new pump in, tank looked clean, new gasket in and pump.

The truck didn't give rpm's after a few tries and I got discouraged. Tried again and again, nothing, battery died. Went and watched a video and realized I needed to keep trying. So had a friend hook up jumper cables and like 10 tries later I got an rpm spike. I must've tried 50 more times after that and the spike never went further, itd just immediate die, I got discouraged again, cursing, calling it quits and my friend just tried I once after I had walked off and it started right up. Like I had warmed up the slot machine and quit and the next guy hit the jackpot.

Anyways, since battery had died I let it idle for a few hours foe the alternator to charge the battery, used the time with the bumper off to beat out a severe dent with a minisledge and propane, turned out nice and straight. While idling it never through any codes so that was it just a pump that worked its last day and decided to die... Putting it back together was way easier.

Itd have been a $800-1000 repair at a shop probably with all that labor, but I never checked, ended up with that part plus the tow to my house ($100). Not bad.
